last.verdict: MetLife posted its best quarter ever, but much of the profit jump came from volatile investment returns rather than steadier insurance operations.

takeaways.label: Record, but investment-boosted
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to a record $2.85, excluding one-time items. Variable investment income, which swings with markets, jumped 49% to $720 million.

takeaways.label: Broad sales growth
takeaways.text: Revenue excluding large pension deals rose 8% to $13.5 billion, with growth in all six segments. Europe, Middle East and Africa earnings rose 30% excluding one-time items. Group Benefits rose 14% on better claims.

takeaways.label: Weak spots underneath
takeaways.text: Latin America earnings excluding one-time items fell 5% after currency effects, on lower investment returns. Asia sales dropped 6%. The share of revenue spent on direct costs rose to 11.9% from 11.6%.

takeaways.label: Net income flattered
takeaways.text: Net income of $3.67 per share, up 201%, was lifted by $698 million of derivative gains from higher interest rates, so adjusted earnings are the better gauge.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
